criteria_details.description: States that Virginia Code § 18.2-47 governs the crime of abduction.

States that under Virginia Code § 18.2-47 any person who 1) by force, intimidation or deception 2) seizes, takes, transports, detains or secretes another person 3) with the intent to deprive such othe
States that a defendant can be convicted of abduction in addition to robbery if the victim's detention is separate and apart from the restraint employed in the commission of robbery.
States that a defendant cannot be convicted of abduction in addition to robbery if the victim's detention is merely incidental to the restraint employed in the commission of robbery.
States that all of the following factors are central to determining whether an abduction is incidental to another crime: 1) the duration of the detention; 2) whether the detention occurred during the
Identifies all of the following as elements of robbery: the taking, with intent to steal, of the personal property of another, from his person or in his presence, against his will, and by violence or
Identifies that Jim told Bobby to lay on the floor after striking Bobby.
Identifies that Jim took Bobby's belongings.
Concludes that Jim is likely to be convicted of robbery for the taking of Bobby's belongings from his person by violence.
Concludes that Bobby's detention was incidental to the crime of robbery against him.
Concludes that Jim is not likely to be convicted of abduction pursuant to Virginia Code § 18.2-47 in relation to Bobby.
Concludes that Jim likely committed robbery of the bank.
Identifies that Jim commanded the Bank teller (Janet) to lay face down on the floor after she put the money in the bag.
Concludes that the bank teller's (Janet's) detention was incidental to the robbery of the bank.
Concludes that Jim is not likely to be convicted of abduction pursuant to Virginia Code 18.2-47 in relation to the Bank teller (Janet).
